subject: Streaming chat p99 spike during night peak - production impact
messages:
From: Claire Johnson <claire.johnson@humboltmedia.com>
To: monica_patel@redwood.com, anton@humboltmedia.com
Date: 2028-05-30T19:12:00-07:00
Subject: Streaming chat severe latency and reconnects tonight

Monica,

We started seeing a large spike in latency on the hosted streaming chat (SSE) at about 18:45 PT — p99 jumped from ~1.2s to ~8s and connection churn spiked. Customer-facing chat sessions are seeing repeated reconnects and a number of messages failing to deliver (we're seeing 502/504 in the client, and some duplicate messages when the client retries). This is exclusively during our evening peak window.

We have a PagerDuty incident open (PTR-4278). Our SREs pulled some early traces and they show long pauses inside the send pipeline around batching and KV cache misses. Throughput (messages/sec) dropped ~25% while errors increased ~6x. This is impacting our homepage chat and a paid campaign bot.

Can Redwood confirm what changed on your side? Was there any model rollout, kernel change, or routing update in the last hour? We need immediate mitigation guidance — ideally a short-term workaround (force non-streaming fallback?) and an ETA for resolution.

Please escalate as needed.

- Claire
Senior Engineering Manager, Humbolt Media

--

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Streaming chat severe latency and reconnects tonight

Quick diagnostic (initial):
- Correlation: spike start at 18:44 PT aligns with an automated kernel selection rollout to a subset of hosts in us-west-2 that adjusted batching thresholds (low risk rollout flagged as "perf-opt-20280530").
- Observed symptoms: sudden increase in batch queue depth + KV cache eviction storms on several streaming shards; worker memory pressure rose and GC pauses increased. End-to-end pipeline shows backpressure at the per-connection send_queue.
- Metrics: streaming-worker CPU near 85%, p99 token latency to send queue rose to 7.9s, errors (502/504/timeouts) up ~6x.

Immediate actions applied (19:40 PT):
1) Rolled back perf-opt-20280530 rollout for streaming hosts (partial rollback initiated).
2) Scaled streaming-worker pool +30% for affected shards (auto-scaling lag is ~3m; forced scale applied).
3) Enabled 10% fallback to long-polling endpoint for sessions started after 19:42 PT (traffic-shift rule ID: shift-20280530-10p).
4) Increased keep-alive & connection window settings to reduce churn (temporary config).

Preliminary result: p99 improved to ~2.3s within ~8 minutes after rollback + scale. Some clients still see reconnects; we suspect residual KV cache rehydration + reactive autoscaling lag.

Next steps:
- Continue scaling until p99 < 1.5s; monitor for stability for 30m.
- Post-incident RCA: investigate kernel selection rollout gating and make rollout canary smaller + longer.
- Consider an emergency rule to route heavy customers to dedicated capacity during peak windows (proposal needed for account team).

PagerDuty: PTR-4278
Confluence playbook: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OPS/pages/Stream+Peak+Playbook

- Rishi
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

What we've done for Humbolt Media:
- Enabled a 10% traffic fallback to polling for the most critical routes (reduces real-time semantics but prevents message loss).
- Added temporary rate smoothing for your busiest bot endpoints to avoid bursts.
- CS will open a follow-up to discuss a short-term credit for the affected windows.

Can we schedule a 30-min post-mortem tomorrow morning to review the root cause and a durable mitigation plan? I'll coordinate with your ops/sre team for a time that works.

Thanks for the patience — we'll keep the bridge open and I'll post updates there.

Claire — quick summary and next steps now that we've stabilized: 

Timeline & outcome:
- 18:44 PT: p99 began climbing after perf-opt-20280530 kernel/batching change partially rolled out.
- 19:40 PT: rollback + scaling + 10% polling fallback applied.
- 19:50 PT: p99 dropped to ~2.3s; by 20:10 PT p99 under 1.5s for the majority of sessions.

Actions we're taking (short and medium term):
- Short: Formalize an emergency routing rule so we can move large customers to dedicated capacity or force polling fallback quicker.
- Medium: Change kernel rollout gating and increase canary length; add an autoscale hysteresis for streaming-worker pool so reactive scale doesn't underprovision.
- Business: Marissa will follow up on a goodwill credit for the impacted window; Aditya (cc'd) will flag this for executive awareness on the account.

Requested from Humbolt (what we need):
- Any client-side SDK logs/examples you can share where the client saw duplicates or timeouts (attach if possible).
- Confirmation of peak windows where you'd like routing to dedicated/priority capacity if we propose it.

We're treating this as a high-priority incident and will publish an RCA by EOD tomorrow. If you prefer, we can schedule an exec sync — Aditya, feel free to advise on whether a 1:1 with Humbolt execs is warranted.

Apologies again — we'll make sure there are concrete changes so this doesn't recur.

— Monica
